open_points.subject: A18 process boundary
open_points.text: “The kernel is one process” conflicts literally with A03’s sandbox execution in a fresh bubblewrap environment whose processes are later reaped.
open_points.question: Does the one-process rule mean one long-lived coordinating kernel process while allowing transient sandbox child processes, or does it prohibit every additional OS process?
options: One kernel process plus transient sandbox processes
Exactly one OS process, including during function execution
open_points.default_guess: Treat sandbox processes as external execution children and permit them while keeping one long-lived kernel process.

open_points.subject: data-directory initialization
open_points.text: “At start it takes an exclusive lock in the data directory” and “The data directory holds one SQLite database …” do not say which missing directories, database, value areas or spool areas the kernel creates.
open_points.question: What must already exist on first start, and what storage structures may the kernel create automatically?
options: Require a pre-created data directory and create its internal layout and database
Create the data directory and all contents
Require the complete layout and database to exist
open_points.default_guess: Require the configured data directory to exist with acceptable ownership and permissions, then create the database and internal subdirectories securely.

open_points.subject: data-directory privacy
open_points.text: “The directory and everything in it are private to the kernel's user” does not define private.
open_points.question: Which ownership, permission, file-type, hard-link and access-control conditions must directories, the database, lock, temporary files, value files, fixtures and spool files satisfy?
options: Require kernel-user ownership and no group/other permissions, with regular files and directories only
Require only that other users cannot currently read the objects
Use platform-specific private-directory checks
open_points.default_guess: Require kernel-user ownership, directories with no group/other permissions, regular files with no group/other permissions, and reject unexpected object types.

open_points.subject: runtime storage safety checks
open_points.text: “The kernel refuses to start otherwise” specifies a start-time privacy check, while only symbolic links receive an explicit later check.
open_points.question: If ownership, permissions, file type or link count becomes unsafe after start, must each affected store call refuse, or are those properties checked only at startup?
options: Revalidate all safety properties on every open
Check privacy and object types only at startup but reject later symbolic links
Assume the data directory cannot change externally while locked
open_points.default_guess: Revalidate ownership, permissions, type and no-follow conditions whenever an object is opened.

open_points.subject: startup check order
open_points.text: A18 separately requires the exclusive lock, privacy checks, symbolic-link scan, database access and cleanup, but gives no order among them.
open_points.question: In what order are A18 startup checks and cleanup performed, and which refusal is returned when several conditions fail?
options: Lock, validate, open database, then clean
Validate before taking the lock
Clean before opening or validating the database
open_points.default_guess: Open the directory safely, acquire the lock, validate the complete layout, open and validate the database, then perform cleanup.

open_points.subject: startup cleanup failure
open_points.text: “On start, temporary files, value bytes no record names … are removed” says only that an unremovable obsolete spool directory does not stop startup.
open_points.question: What happens when a temporary file or an unreferenced value byte file cannot be inspected or removed?
options: Refuse startup
Continue startup and leave it unserved
Quarantine it and continue
open_points.default_guess: Refuse startup because the text grants continue-on-failure only for obsolete spool directories.

open_points.subject: database validity and compatibility
open_points.text: “The data directory holds one SQLite database with every kernel record” does not state what happens when the database is absent, corrupt, has an unknown schema version or contains inconsistent records.
open_points.question: Which database states initialize a new store, which are migrated, and which refuse startup without modifying existing data?
options: Create only when absent; refuse corruption and unknown schemas
Recreate any unreadable or incompatible database
Automatically migrate recognized older schemas and refuse unknown ones
open_points.default_guess: Create a database only when absent; refuse corruption, inconsistency and unsupported schema versions without modifying the existing store.

open_points.subject: surface request serialization
open_points.text: “Surface requests are handled one at a time in the order they arrive” does not define arrival when requests reach the MCP server concurrently.
open_points.question: What event establishes the total arrival order, and are later concurrent requests queued or refused while one request is running?
options: Assign a sequence when the server accepts each complete request and queue it
Order by connection acceptance
Refuse requests received while another is running
open_points.default_guess: Assign a monotonic sequence when a complete request enters the kernel and process queued requests by that sequence.

open_points.subject: store record order
open_points.text: “Activation M09 and FlowActivation M18 records are identified by their position in the store's one order of records” does not define how that order is assigned when one transaction creates several records or updates an existing entity.
open_points.question: Does every newly created durable record receive a unique global position, what is the order of multiple creations in one transaction, and does updating a record preserve or change its position?
options: One immutable global creation position per record, with an explicit within-transaction insertion order
One position per transaction shared by its records
Updates receive new positions
open_points.default_guess: Give every created record a unique monotonically increasing position in its specified write order, and preserve that position through later status updates.

open_points.subject: store-call transaction boundaries
open_points.text: “Every change is one call to the store module and one transaction inside it” does not define which records and state transitions constitute one change for actions that create or update several records.
open_points.question: For each multi-record action, which writes must commit atomically and which may remain committed if a later write in the same surface request fails or the process crashes?
options: The entire surface action is one store call and transaction
Each individual record mutation is a separate store call
Use explicit decision-specific atomic groups
open_points.default_guess: Use decision-specific atomic groups where the text explicitly says records change together, and separate calls for explicitly staged work such as in-flight and outcome recording.

open_points.subject: database and file crash consistency
open_points.text: “Value bytes and spooled files are written to a temporary file, flushed, checked … and then renamed into place” does not define the durability ordering between file rename, directory metadata and the SQLite commit.
open_points.question: After an acknowledged store call or a crash at any point, may a committed record name missing bytes, and what file and directory synchronization must precede the database commit?
options: A committed record may never name missing or incomplete bytes
Only process-crash atomicity is promised, not host-crash durability
SQLite and files may recover independently, with missing bytes handled later
open_points.default_guess: Publish and durably synchronize the file and parent directory before committing any record that names it, so committed records never reference missing or incomplete bytes.

open_points.subject: late symbolic-link failure
open_points.text: Rule 2 says “one found later makes that store call fail with nothing written,” while rule 3 says a failed call may leave “a published file no record names.”
open_points.question: May a store call that encounters a symbolic link leave an unreferenced published file, or must it leave no filesystem artifact at all?
options: No record or filesystem artifact may remain
An unreferenced published file may remain under rule 3
Only artifacts created before encountering the link may remain
open_points.default_guess: Treat the specific symbolic-link rule as stronger: the call leaves neither record changes nor published filesystem artifacts.
